question.problem: An ink reservoir for an industrial printer can hold up to $150\,\text{gal}$ of liquid. Initially, it contains $60\,\text{gal}$ of ink solution with $18\,\text{lb}$ of dissolved ink dye. A more concentrated ink solution with concentration $\frac{4}{3}\,\text{lb/gal}$ flows into the reservoir at a rate of $9\,\text{gal/min},$ while the completely mixed solution drains out at a rate of $6\,\text{gal/min}.$ Rounded to one decimal place, find the amount of ink dye in the reservoir at the moment it begins to overflow.
question.worked_solution:
Since $Q$ is the amount of ink dye in the reservoir at time $t,$ the derivative 

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}
$$

describes how this amount changes with respect to time $t,$ in minutes. This is equal to the rate at which ink dye enters the reservoir minus the rate at which ink dye leaves the reservoir.

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}
$$

Note that the units of $\frac{dQ}{dt},{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}$ and ${Q}_{\text{out}}^{′}$ are $\text{lb}/\text{min}.$ Now, let's compute the required rates of change in steps.

**Step 1**: Calculating the rate at which ink dye enters the reservoir.

First, note that a solution containing $\frac{4}{3}\,\text{lb/gal}$ of ink dye enters the reservoir at a rate of $9\,\text{gal/min}.$ So, the rate at which the *ink dye* enters the reservoir is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{in}}^{′} & =(\frac{4}{3}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}})\cdot (9\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =(\frac{4}{3}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}})\cdot (9\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}}) \\  & =12\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 2**: Calculating the rate at which ink dye exits the reservoir.

To find the rate at which ink dye leaves the reservoir, we must first determine the volume of solution in the reservoir at time $t.$

The reservoir initially contains $60\,\text{gal}$ of solution; solution enters at $9\,\text{gal/min}$ and mixed solution leaves at $6\,\text{gal/min}.$
As a result, the amount of solution in the reservoir after $t$ minutes is 

$$
V(t)=60+9t-6t=3(20+t)\,\text{gal}.
$$

Note that $V(t)$ is an increasing function, so the reservoir is filling.

Since $Q$ is the amount of ink dye in the reservoir, the concentration of the solution at time $t$ is

$$
\frac{Q}{3(20+t)}\,\text{lb/gal}.
$$

Therefore, as the completely mixed solution leaves at a rate of $6\,\text{gal/min},$ *ink dye* leaves at a rate of

$$
\begin{aligned}{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} & =(6\,\frac{\text{gal}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{3(20+t)}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{gal}}) \\  & =(6\,\frac{\cancel{\text{gal}}}{\text{min}})\cdot (\frac{Q}{3(20+t)}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\cancel{\text{gal}}}) \\  & =\frac{6Q}{3(20+t)}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}} \\  & =\frac{2Q}{20+t}\,\frac{\text{lb}}{\text{min}}.\end{aligned}
$$

**Step 3**: Calculate the overall rate of change.

The rate of change equals the rate of entry minus the rate of exit. Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{dQ}{dt} & ={Q}_{\text{in}}^{′}-{Q}_{\text{out}}^{′} \\  & =12-\frac{2Q}{20+t}\end{aligned}
$$

which gives the equation

$$
\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{20+t}\,Q=12.
$$

**Step 4**: Integrate the equation.

This is a first-order linear equation with variable coefficients. So we find the general solution using an integrating factor:

$$
\begin{aligned}I(t) & ={e}^{\int 2/(20+t)\,dt} \\  & ={e}^{2\operatorname{ln}⁡|20+t|} \\  & ={e}^{\operatorname{ln}⁡(20+t)^{2}} \\  & =(20+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides of the differential equation by $I(t)=(20+t)^{2}$ yields

$$
\begin{aligned}(20+t)^{2}\cdot (\frac{dQ}{dt}+\frac{2}{20+t}\,Q) & =(20+t)^{2}\cdot 12 \\ (20+t)^{2}\frac{dQ}{dt}+2(20+t)Q & =12(20+t)^{2} \\ \frac{d}{dt}(Q(20+t)^{2}) & =12(20+t)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we integrate with respect to $t:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{d}{dt}(Q(20+t)^{2})\,dt & =\int 12(20+t)^{2}\,dt \\ Q(20+t)^{2} & =12\cdot \frac{1}{3}(20+t)^{3}+C \\ Q(t) & =4(20+t)+\frac{C}{(20+t)^{2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

We're told that the reservoir initially contains $18\,\text{lb}$ of ink dye. So, we can apply the initial condition $Q(0)=18,$ and solve for $C:$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(0) & =18 \\ 4(20+0)+\frac{C}{(20+0)^{2}} & =18 \\ 80+\frac{C}{(20)^{2}} & =18 \\ \frac{C}{{20}^{2}} & =-62 \\ C & =-62(20)^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain the following expression for $Q(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(t) & =4(20+t)-\frac{62(20)^{2}}{(20+t)^{2}} \\  & =4(20+t)-62{(\frac{20}{20+t})}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let ${t}_{o}$ be the time when the reservoir begins to overflow. The reservoir has a capacity of $150\,\text{gal},$ so we can use the condition $V({t}_{o})=150$ to solve for ${t}_{o}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}V({t}_{o}) & =150 \\ 60+9{t}_{o}-6{t}_{o} & =150 \\ 60+3{t}_{o} & =150 \\ 3{t}_{o} & =90 \\ {t}_{o} & =30\,\text{min}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, rounded to one decimal place, the amount of ink dye in the reservoir at the moment it begins to overflow is

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(30) & =4(20+30)-62{(\frac{20}{20+30})}^{2} \\  & =200-62{(\frac{20}{50})}^{2} \\  & ≈190.1\,\text{lb}.\end{aligned}
$$
